name: The Politics of AI
blurb: Who in government is doing what about AI, shown through the public record rather than rhetoric: the positions lawmakers take by their votes and bills, the money that reaches them from AI companies and AI-focused political committees, the lobbying filed on AI, how often an AI issue moves from a bill to a law, the federal effort to override state AI laws, and what members say beside how they vote. Every entry cites the filing, vote or statement it rests on. The site records the record and leaves the reader to judge motive.

items.claim: Originality.ai classified 2,099 of 21,388 House and Senate floor turns of over 100 words (2025 to 17 August 2026) as likely AI written. The rate rose from 8.4 percent in 2025 to 12.2 percent in 2026 to date, against about 2 percent in 2020; in 2025 the House ran at 11.4 percent and the Senate at 3.1 percent, and in 2026 Republican members were 7.9 points above their 2025 rate and Democrats 4.3 points. Each turn was classified whole by Originality.ai Lite (AI allowance 15, confidence 0.50 or higher), so these are shares of speeches, not of words.
items.source_title: Originality.ai, Likely AI Language Surged Across the Congressional Record

items.claim: The offices of Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks and Rep. Mike Lawler confirmed on the record that AI tools are used in drafting. AI text detectors are statistical and cannot explain why a passage is classified; Hany Farid of Dartmouth made that point to the Post, and two detectors disagreed on 3 of a random sample of classified turns.
items.source_title: Washington Post AI and Tech Brief, 2026-10-07, on the Originality.ai report

items.claim: Rep. Lori Trahan (D-MA) released a discussion draft of the Clear Liability for Artificial Intelligence Misconduct (CLAIM) Act on 7 October 2026. A developer would be liable when its AI system injures a third party through conduct that would be negligence, an intentional tort or a crime if a person did it, with courts presuming the system had the state of mind a person taking the same actions would have; claims could be brought in federal or state court, and the Act sets a federal floor rather than preempting state law. It is a draft for comment, with no bill number, and is framed as a companion to the FRONTIER Act she introduced with Rep. Jay Obernolte.
items.source_title: Rep. Trahan press release, CLAIM Act discussion draft

items.claim: Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-WA), ranking member of Senate Commerce, published a six-principle governance framework for frontier AI on 7 October 2026: enforceable NIST standards with independent audit before a covered model is released, heightened review of systems with dangerous capabilities or that can self-improve past their safety controls, prompt reporting of material safety and security incidents including loss of control over autonomous agents, transparency with liability, public-private work on defensive AI, protections for children and workers, and a US-led push for common international standards. It also proposes a secure channel with China, on the model of the Cold War hotline, for significant AI incidents that could threaten either country.
items.source_title: Senate Commerce Committee (Democrats), Cantwell Outlines Comprehensive Governance Framework for Safe and Secure Frontier AI
